# Zombie Escape

A 7-day winter escape across the U.S. Real county populations, real January weather, real road distances; a fictional zombie. Version 3 sets each county's starting infection from when you arrive (5% on Day 1 rising to 35% on Day 7, ±10 points for density; see docs/MATH.md §13). Version 2 added the revised scenarios (140 scenes, 5 real-data events, 10 realistic mini games), CDC SVI 2022 data, a status dashboard between scenes, pause, metric units and a password-protected developer mode.

## Requirements

- **Python 3.10+.** The game, the console version and the server use only the standard library.
- For the tests and the survival report: `pip install -r requirements.txt` (pytest, matplotlib).
- Optional: Node.js 18+ for the Python-vs-JavaScript parity test; `pip install playwright` + Chrome for the browser playthrough test.

## Run it

```bash
# Browser game on this computer
python server.py                       # open http://localhost:8000

# Host it for others on your network (no domain needed)
python server.py --host 0.0.0.0        # prints http://<your-ip>:8000

# Console game
python play.py                         # pick a city
python play.py --city NYC --seed 42 --debug     # show every calculation
python play.py --city SEA --auto balanced       # watch an AI strategy play
```

Opening `web/index.html` directly in a browser also works (no server needed).

### Hosting without registering a domain

| Option | What to do | Address people use |
|---|---|---|
| Your own computer, same Wi-Fi | `python server.py --host 0.0.0.0` (allow Python through the firewall if asked) | `http://192.168.x.x:8000` |
| A cloud virtual machine | Copy the folder, run `python server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` (or `docker build -t zombie . && docker run -p 8000:8000 zombie`), open port 8000 in the VM's firewall | `http://<VM public IP>:8000` |
| Any static host | Upload the `web/` folder as is (it's plain HTML/JS); the `/api/montecarlo` endpoint is the only part that needs `server.py` | the host's free subdomain |

The server also has `/health` (returns `ok`) and `/api/montecarlo?city=NYC&policy=balanced&runs=500`.

## Play it on GitHub Pages (free, no domain)

In the repository: **Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from a branch → Branch: main, folder: / (root) → Save.**
After a minute the game is live at `https://<username>.github.io/<repo-name>/`. The root `index.html` sends visitors to `web/index.html`.
(The `/api/montecarlo` endpoint needs `server.py`; everything else, including the in-browser Monte Carlo, works on Pages.)

## Tests

```bash
python tools/build_web.py              # rebuild web/data.js + tests/bundle.json
python -m pytest -q tests              # 75 tests: data, SEIR, game rules, Monte Carlo, Python/JS parity, server
python tests/browser_playthrough.py    # optional: plays all 7 routes in headless Chrome
```

## Survival report

```bash
python tools/monte_carlo_report.py --runs 1000     # about 4 minutes
```

Writes `reports/survival_report.md` with charts, decision impact, the dominance check and SEIR sensitivity.

## Playing (version 2)

| Feature | How it works |
|---|---|
| Status dashboard | After each choice, one screen shows your stats with +/− changes, the outcome rating (BEST / OKAY / RISKY / BAD), why health changed, and the drive. **One Enter** moves on. |
| Pause | **P** or the Pause button stops the 20-second timer and hides the options. After you resume, pause is locked for 30 seconds. |
| Units | "Metric units" on the title screen, or the °F/°C button in the top bar: °C, km, liters (story text too). |
| Player mode | No ratings, no formulas, no SEIR numbers during play. The SEIR model, every health loss with its reason, and R0 vs real diseases appear on the end screen. |
| Developer mode | Enter the team password on the title screen. No timer; option ratings, every calculation, the SEIR panel, live multipliers and "How it's built" code notes. The page stores only a SHA-256 hash of the password. This is a convenience lock, not security: anyone who reads the code can turn it on. |
| Option letters | A–D always; E = unlocked by an earlier choice; F/G = only in certain conditions (low fuel, symptoms, behind schedule, low health); R = rest. Keys: the letter or 1–7. |

## Data added in version 2

`data/svi_data.csv` (CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022, county: overall SVI, % aged 65+, % households without a vehicle), `data/r0_reference.csv` and `data/rabies_reference.csv` (published values, cited). `python tools/download_new_data.py` rebuilds them. The Census ACS API now needs a key, so age structure comes from the SVI file's ACS 2018–2022 column instead of a separate `age_data.csv`.

## Documentation

- `docs/AUDIT.md`: what the game was, what was wrong, what changed
- `docs/MATH.md`: every formula, labeled REAL / FICTIONAL / CALCULATED / DECISION
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: files and data flow
- `data/data_sources.md`: where every number came from, what is missing and how to add it
- `docs/PRESENTATION.md`: talking points for presenting the project
- `docs/word/Zombie_Escape_Game_Breakdown.docx`: every part of the game in tables
- `docs/word/Zombie_Escape_Revised_Scenarios.docx`: all 140 scenes with the 10 improvements and 10 realistic mini games (now in the game: content/scenarios_v2.json)
- `scenario_revisions/`: the scripts that build the revised scenario doc
- `web/zombie_escape_full_game.html`: the whole browser game in one file (double-click to play)

FILE: minigames.py

"""
Zombie Escape - mini games.

LIVE versions use Python's built-in `curses` module: things move on screen in real
time and react to your keypresses. They run in a real terminal window:
  * Mac / Linux: works as-is (Terminal app).
  * Windows: run `pip install windows-curses` once, then use Command Prompt or PowerShell.
If curses can't start (IDLE, Colab, a window that's too small), each game automatically
switches to its TEXT version so the game never crashes.

Every game: play(name, tier) -> (won: bool, bonus: dict)
tier is "HARD", "NORMAL" or "EASY". bonus can hold extra supplies earned live, e.g. {"water": 10}.
"""
import random
import sys
import time

try:
    import curses
except ImportError:          # Windows without windows-curses
    curses = None


class TooSmall(Exception):
    pass


# ======================================================================
# Shared helpers for live games
# ======================================================================
def _setup(scr, rows=22, cols=64):
    h, w = scr.getmaxyx()
    if h < rows or w < cols:
        raise TooSmall()
    curses.curs_set(0)
    scr.keypad(True)
    scr.nodelay(True)
    if curses.has_colors():
        curses.start_color()
        try:
            curses.use_default_colors()
            bg = -1
        except curses.error:
            bg = curses.COLOR_BLACK
        curses.init_pair(1, curses.COLOR_GREEN, bg)
        curses.init_pair(2, curses.COLOR_RED, bg)
        curses.init_pair(3, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, bg)
        curses.init_pair(4, curses.COLOR_CYAN, bg)
        curses.init_pair(5, curses.COLOR_BLUE, bg)


def C(n):
    return curses.color_pair(n) if curses.has_colors() else 0


def put(scr, y, x, s, attr=0):
    try:
        scr.addstr(y, x, s, attr)
    except curses.error:
        pass


def flush(scr):
    while scr.getch() != -1:
        pass


def intro(scr, title, tier, lines):
    scr.nodelay(False)
    scr.timeout(20000)                      # wait up to 20 s on the instructions
    scr.erase()
    color = {"HARD": C(2), "NORMAL": C(3), "EASY": C(1)}[tier]
    put(scr, 1, 2, f"MINI GAME: {title}", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
    put(scr, 2, 2, f"Difficulty: {tier}", curses.A_BOLD | color)
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        put(scr, 4 + i, 4, line)
    put(scr, 5 + len(lines), 4, "Press any key to start...", C(3))
    scr.refresh()
    scr.getch()
    for n in ("3", "2", "1", "GO!"):
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 9, 28, n, curses.A_BOLD | C(3))
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.5)
    scr.nodelay(True)
    scr.timeout(0)
    flush(scr)


def outro(scr, won, msg=""):
    scr.erase()
    put(scr, 8, 24, "SUCCESS!" if won else "FAILED!", curses.A_BOLD | (C(1) if won else C(2)))
    if msg:
        put(scr, 10, 6, msg)
    scr.refresh()
    time.sleep(1.8)


def timer_bar(scr, y, x, left, total, width=30):
    frac = max(0.0, min(1.0, left / total))
    filled = int(frac * width)
    color = C(1) if frac > 0.5 else C(3) if frac > 0.25 else C(2)
    put(scr, y, x, "TIME [")
    put(scr, y, x + 6, "#" * filled, color | curses.A_BOLD)
    put(scr, y, x + 6 + filled, "-" * (width - filled))
    put(scr, y, x + 6 + width, f"] {max(0, left):4.1f}s")


def read_key_into(scr, buf, allowed):
    """Collect typed keys into a buffer. Returns (buf, entered)."""
    entered = False
    k = scr.getch()
    while k != -1:
        if k in (10, 13, curses.KEY_ENTER):
            entered = True
        elif k in (8, 127, curses.KEY_BACKSPACE):
            buf = buf[:-1]
        elif 0 <= k < 256 and chr(k).upper() in allowed and len(buf) < 20:
            buf += chr(k).upper()
        k = scr.getch()
    return buf, entered


# ======================================================================
# 1. LOCK THE DOOR (live timing bar)
# ======================================================================
LOCK = {"HARD": (3, 44), "NORMAL": (5, 30), "EASY": (9, 20)}   # green zone width, marker speed


def live_lock_door(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    zone, speed = LOCK[tier]
    intro(scr, "Lock the Door", tier, [
        "The infected are slamming against the door!",
        "A marker slides back and forth across the lock bar.",
        "Press SPACE when the marker is inside the GREEN zone.",
        "3 rounds. Lock it 2 times to win."])
    W, wins = 44, 0
    for rnd in range(1, 4):
        start = random.randint(8, W - zone - 2)
        pos, direction, passes, result = 0.0, 1, 0, None
        last = time.monotonic()
        while result is None:
            now = time.monotonic()
            pos += direction * speed * (now - last)
            last = now
            if pos >= W - 1:
                pos, direction, passes = W - 1, -1, passes + 1
            elif pos <= 0:
                pos, direction, passes = 0, 1, passes + 1
            if passes >= 4:
                result = False
            if scr.getch() == ord(" "):
                result = start <= int(pos) < start + zone
            scr.erase()
            put(scr, 1, 2, f"LOCK THE DOOR   Round {rnd}/3   Locks: {wins}", curses.A_BOLD)
            put(scr, 4, 4, "BANG! BANG!" if int(now * 3) % 2 else "", C(2) | curses.A_BOLD)
            put(scr, 7, 4, "[")
            for i in range(W):
                in_zone = start <= i < start + zone
                put(scr, 7, 5 + i, "=" if in_zone else "-", (C(1) | curses.A_BOLD) if in_zone else 0)
            put(scr, 7, 5 + W, "]")
            put(scr, 6, 5 + int(pos), "v", C(3) | curses.A_BOLD)
            put(scr, 8, 5 + int(pos), "^", C(3) | curses.A_BOLD)
            put(scr, 11, 4, "Press SPACE in the green zone!")
            scr.refresh()
            time.sleep(0.016)
        wins += bool(result)
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 9, 8, "LOCKED!" if result else "MISSED! The door cracks open...",
            curses.A_BOLD | (C(1) if result else C(2)))
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.9)
        flush(scr)
        if wins >= 2 or rnd - wins >= 2:
            break
    won = wins >= 2
    outro(scr, won)
    return won, {}


# ======================================================================
# 2. ESCAPE THE HORDE (live chase on a grid)
# ======================================================================
HORDE = {"HARD": (5, 0.33, 25), "NORMAL": (3, 0.5, 30), "EASY": (2, 0.8, 40)}  # zombies, step time, seconds


def _path_exists(grid, a, b):
    seen, todo = {a}, [a]
    while todo:
        y, x = todo.pop()
        if (y, x) == b:
            return True
        for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
            ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
            if 0 <= ny < len(grid) and 0 <= nx < len(grid[0]) and grid[ny][nx] != "#" and (ny, nx) not in seen:
                seen.add((ny, nx))
                todo.append((ny, nx))
    return False


def _zombie_step(grid, z, p, taken):
    options = []
    for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
        ny, nx = z[0] + dy, z[1] + dx
        if 0 <= ny < len(grid) and 0 <= nx < len(grid[0]) and grid[ny][nx] != "#" \
                and ((ny, nx) not in taken or (ny, nx) == p):
            options.append((abs(ny - p[0]) + abs(nx - p[1]), random.random(), (ny, nx)))
    if not options:
        return z
    if random.random() < 0.2:                         # zombies stumble sometimes
        return random.choice(options)[2]
    return min(options)[2]


def live_escape_horde(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    nz, step, limit = HORDE[tier]
    intro(scr, "Escape the Horde", tier, [
        "You're trapped in a parking lot full of wrecked cars (#).",
        "Move with the ARROW KEYS or W A S D.",
        "Reach the exit E before the infected Z catch you.",
        f"{nz} infected are hunting you. You have {limit} seconds."])
    GW, GH = 40, 14
    while True:
        grid = [["#" if random.random() < 0.18 else " " for _ in range(GW)] for _ in range(GH)]
        p, e = (GH // 2, 1), (random.randint(1, GH - 2), GW - 2)
        grid[p[0]][p[1]] = grid[e[0]][e[1]] = " "
        if _path_exists(grid, p, e):
            break
    zs = []
    while len(zs) < nz:
        z = (random.randint(0, GH - 1), random.randint(GW // 3, GW - 4))
        if grid[z[0]][z[1]] == " " and z != e and z not in zs:
            zs.append(z)
    moves = {curses.KEY_UP: (-1, 0), curses.KEY_DOWN: (1, 0), curses.KEY_LEFT: (0, -1), curses.KEY_RIGHT: (0, 1)}
    for ch, mv in (("w", (-1, 0)), ("s", (1, 0)), ("a", (0, -1)), ("d", (0, 1))):
        moves[ord(ch)] = moves[ord(ch.upper())] = mv
    t0 = last_z = time.monotonic()
    result = None
    while result is None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        k = scr.getch()
        while k != -1:
            if k in moves:
                dy, dx = moves[k]
                ny, nx = p[0] + dy, p[1] + dx
                if 0 <= ny < GH and 0 <= nx < GW and grid[ny][nx] != "#":
                    p = (ny, nx)
            k = scr.getch()
        if p == e:
            result = True
        elif now - last_z >= step:
            last_z = now
            zs = [_zombie_step(grid, z, p, set(zs)) for z in zs]
        if result is None and (p in zs or now - t0 > limit):
            result = False
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 1, 2, "ESCAPE THE HORDE", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
        timer_bar(scr, 2, 2, limit - (now - t0), limit)
        oy, ox = 4, 4
        put(scr, oy - 1, ox - 1, "+" + "-" * GW + "+")
        put(scr, oy + GH, ox - 1, "+" + "-" * GW + "+")
        for y in range(GH):
            put(scr, oy + y, ox - 1, "|")
            put(scr, oy + y, ox + GW, "|")
            for x in range(GW):
                if grid[y][x] == "#":
                    put(scr, oy + y, ox + x, "#", C(5))
        put(scr, oy + e[0], ox + e[1], "E", C(1) | curses.A_BOLD)
        for z in zs:
            put(scr, oy + z[0], ox + z[1], "Z", C(2) | curses.A_BOLD)
        put(scr, oy + p[0], ox + p[1], "@", C(3) | curses.A_BOLD)
        put(scr, oy + GH + 1, ox, "You = @   Exit = E   Infected = Z")
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.02)
    outro(scr, result, "You slipped out of the lot!" if result else "They caught up to you...")
    return result, {}


# ======================================================================
# 3. DODGE THE WRECKS (live lane driving, grab water bottles)
# ======================================================================
DODGE = {"HARD": (0.09, 20, 1), "NORMAL": (0.14, 16, 2), "EASY": (0.2, 12, 3)}  # tick, seconds, hits allowed


def live_dodge(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    tick, duration, lives = DODGE[tier]
    intro(scr, "Dodge the Wrecks", tier, [
        "You're racing down a jammed highway at night.",
        "LEFT / RIGHT arrows (or A / D) switch lanes.",
        "Dodge wrecks # and infected Z. Grab water bottles W for bonus water!",
        f"Survive {duration} seconds. You can take {lives} hit(s)."])
    H, car_row, lane = 16, 14, 1
    objs, hits, bottles, cooldown = [], 0, 0, 0
    t0 = last = time.monotonic()
    result = None

    def collide():
        nonlocal hits, bottles
        for o in objs[:]:
            if o[0] == car_row and o[1] == lane:
                if o[2] == "W":
                    bottles += 1
                else:
                    hits += 1
                objs.remove(o)

    while result is None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        k = scr.getch()
        while k != -1:
            if k in (curses.KEY_LEFT, ord("a"), ord("A")):
                lane = max(0, lane - 1)
                collide()
            elif k in (curses.KEY_RIGHT, ord("d"), ord("D")):
                lane = min(2, lane + 1)
                collide()
            k = scr.getch()
        if now - last >= tick:
            last = now
            for o in objs:
                o[0] += 1
            collide()
            objs[:] = [o for o in objs if o[0] <= car_row]
            cooldown -= 1
            if cooldown <= 0:
                lanes = [0, 1, 2]
                random.shuffle(lanes)
                for l in lanes[:1 if random.random() < 0.65 else 2]:     # never block all 3 lanes
                    objs.append([0, l, random.choice("##Z")])
                if random.random() < 0.3:
                    objs.append([0, lanes[2], "W"])
                cooldown = random.randint(3, 5)
        if hits >= lives:
            result = False
        elif now - t0 >= duration:
            result = True
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 1, 2, "DODGE THE WRECKS", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
        timer_bar(scr, 2, 2, duration - (now - t0), duration)
        put(scr, 3, 2, f"Hits: {hits}/{lives}    Water bottles: {bottles}")
        ox = 20
        for r in range(H):
            put(scr, 5 + r, ox, "|      :      :      |")
        for row, l, kind in objs:
            color = C(2) if kind == "Z" else C(4) if kind == "W" else C(5)
            put(scr, 5 + row, ox + 3 + l * 7, kind, color | curses.A_BOLD)
        put(scr, 5 + car_row, ox + 2 + lane * 7, "[A]", C(3) | curses.A_BOLD)
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.015)
    outro(scr, result, f"You grabbed {bottles} water bottle(s)." if bottles else "")
    return result, ({"water": 5 * bottles} if bottles else {})


# ======================================================================
# 4. BARRICADE THE DOOR (live falling words)
# ======================================================================
BARRICADE = {"HARD": (0.55, 0), "NORMAL": (0.8, 1), "EASY": (1.15, 2)}   # seconds per row, breaches allowed
WORDS = ["BOARD", "NAIL", "BRACE", "LOCK", "CHAIN", "WEDGE", "BOLT", "PLANK", "HAMMER", "SCREW", "BEAM", "DOOR"]


def live_barricade(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    fall, allowed = BARRICADE[tier]
    need = 6
    intro(scr, "Barricade the Door", tier, [
        "The infected are tearing at the boards!",
        "Words fall toward the door. TYPE a word to nail it in place.",
        "(It locks in as soon as you finish typing it. BACKSPACE fixes typos.)",
        f"Nail {need} words. Breaches allowed: {allowed}."])
    H, active, buf, done, breaches = 13, [], "", 0, 0
    last_fall = next_spawn = time.monotonic()
    result = None
    while result is None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        buf, entered = read_key_into(scr, buf, "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")
        for w in active[:]:
            if buf == w[0]:
                active.remove(w)
                done += 1
                buf = ""
                break
        if entered:
            buf = ""
        if now - last_fall >= fall:
            last_fall = now
            for w in active:
                w[1] += 1
            for w in [w for w in active if w[1] >= H]:
                active.remove(w)
                breaches += 1
        if now >= next_spawn and len(active) < 3:
            word = random.choice([w for w in WORDS if w not in [a[0] for a in active]])
            active.append([word, 0, random.randint(2, 40)])
            next_spawn = now + fall * random.uniform(3, 5)
        if done >= need:
            result = True
        elif breaches > allowed:
            result = False
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 1, 2, f"BARRICADE THE DOOR   Nailed: {done}/{need}   Breaches: {breaches}/{allowed}",
            curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
        for word, row, col in active:
            near = row >= H - 4
            put(scr, 3 + row, 6 + col, word, curses.A_BOLD | (C(2) if near else C(3)))
        put(scr, 3 + H, 4, "=" * 54, C(5) | curses.A_BOLD)
        put(scr, 4 + H, 4, "DOOR", C(5))
        put(scr, 6 + H, 4, f"Typing: {buf}_", curses.A_BOLD)
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.02)
    outro(scr, result)
    return result, {}


# ======================================================================
# 5. SAFE OR UNSAFE? (live conveyor)
# ======================================================================
SAFE_UNSAFE = [
    ("A bulging, swollen can of beans", "U"), ("Snow melted and boiled", "S"),
    ("Water from a red mine pit lake", "U"), ("A sealed bottle of water", "S"),
    ("A rusty, leaking can of soup", "U"), ("A chocolate bar from a gas station", "S"),
    ("Lake water you didn't boil", "U"), ("A jar of honey from a pantry", "S"),
    ("Raw meat from a truck that thawed days ago", "U"), ("A sealed pack of crackers", "S"),
    ("Eating snow instead of melting it first", "U"), ("Water from a home's water heater tank", "S"),
]
CONVEYOR = {"HARD": 13, "NORMAL": 8, "EASY": 5}     # cells per second


def live_safe_unsafe(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    speed = CONVEYOR[tier]
    items, need, right = random.sample(SAFE_UNSAFE, 5), 4, 0
    intro(scr, "Safe or Unsafe?", tier, [
        "Supplies slide down a conveyor toward your backpack.",
        "Press S if the item is SAFE to eat or drink, U if it's UNSAFE.",
        "Decide before it falls off the end!",
        f"Get {need} of 5 right."])
    track = 46
    for n, (text, truth) in enumerate(items, 1):
        x, answer = float(track), None
        last = time.monotonic()
        while answer is None:
            now = time.monotonic()
            x -= speed * (now - last)
            last = now
            k = scr.getch()
            while k != -1:
                if k in (ord("s"), ord("S")):
                    answer = "S"
                elif k in (ord("u"), ord("U")):
                    answer = "U"
                k = scr.getch()
            if x <= 0 and answer is None:
                answer = "-"
            scr.erase()
            put(scr, 1, 2, f"SAFE OR UNSAFE?   Item {n}/5   Correct: {right}", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
            put(scr, 5, 4, text, curses.A_BOLD | C(3))
            put(scr, 8, 4, "[PACK]" + "_" * track)
            put(scr, 7, 10 + int(max(0, x)), "[?]", C(3) | curses.A_BOLD)
            put(scr, 11, 4, "S = SAFE     U = UNSAFE")
            scr.refresh()
            time.sleep(0.016)
        ok = answer == truth
        right += ok
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 5, 4, text, curses.A_BOLD)
        verdict = "SAFE" if truth == "S" else "UNSAFE"
        msg = f"Correct! It's {verdict}." if ok else ("Too slow! " if answer == "-" else "Wrong! ") + f"It's {verdict}."
        put(scr, 8, 4, msg, curses.A_BOLD | (C(1) if ok else C(2)))
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(1.1)
        flush(scr)
    won = right >= need
    outro(scr, won, f"{right} of 5 correct.")
    return won, {}


# ======================================================================
# 6. COUNT THE INFECTED (live march across the screen)
# ======================================================================
MARCH = {"HARD": 26, "NORMAL": 17, "EASY": 10}      # cells per second


def _ask_number(scr, prompt, y):
    scr.nodelay(True)
    buf, entered = "", False
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
    while not entered and time.monotonic() < deadline:
        buf, entered = read_key_into(scr, buf, "0123456789")
        put(scr, y, 4, " " * 50)
        put(scr, y, 4, f"{prompt} {buf}_", curses.A_BOLD)
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.03)
    return int(buf) if buf.isdigit() else -1


def live_count(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    speed = MARCH[tier]
    intro(scr, "Count the Infected", tier, [
        "A crowd is shuffling past your hiding spot.",
        "Count ONLY the infected (Z). Ignore the survivors (H).",
        "After they pass, type your count and press ENTER.",
        "2 rounds. You need to be within 2 both times."])
    width = 50
    for rnd in (1, 2):
        nz, nh, length = random.randint(7, 14), random.randint(4, 8), 70
        stream = {}
        spots = random.sample([(r, c) for r in range(3) for c in range(length)], nz + nh)
        for i, s in enumerate(spots):
            stream[s] = "Z" if i < nz else "H"
        offset = -float(width)
        last = time.monotonic()
        while offset < length:
            now = time.monotonic()
            offset += speed * (now - last)
            last = now
            scr.erase()
            put(scr, 1, 2, f"COUNT THE INFECTED   Round {rnd}/2", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
            put(scr, 4, 4, "=" * (width + 2), C(5))
            put(scr, 8, 4, "=" * (width + 2), C(5))
            for (r, c), kind in stream.items():
                sx = c - int(offset)
                if 0 <= sx < width:
                    put(scr, 5 + r, 5 + (width - 1 - sx), kind, curses.A_BOLD | (C(2) if kind == "Z" else C(1)))
            scr.refresh()
            time.sleep(0.02)
            flush(scr)
        guess = _ask_number(scr, "How many infected (Z)?", 11)
        ok = abs(guess - nz) <= 2
        put(scr, 13, 4, f"There were {nz}. " + ("Close enough!" if ok else "Not close enough."),
            curses.A_BOLD | (C(1) if ok else C(2)))
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(1.3)
        if not ok:
            outro(scr, False)
            return False, {}
    outro(scr, True)
    return True, {}


# ======================================================================
# 7. CRACK THE SUPPLY LOCKER (live countdown, footsteps approach)
# ======================================================================
LOCKER = {"HARD": (4, 15), "NORMAL": (5, 25), "EASY": (6, 45)}   # guesses, seconds


def live_locker(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    tries, limit = LOCKER[tier]
    code = random.randint(1, 20)
    intro(scr, "Crack the Supply Locker", tier, [
        "A locked supply cabinet. Footsteps are getting closer...",
        "The code is a number from 1 to 20.",
        "Type a guess and press ENTER. You'll hear HIGHER or LOWER.",
        f"{tries} guesses, {limit} seconds."])
    t0, buf, log, result = time.monotonic(), "", [], None
    while result is None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        buf, entered = read_key_into(scr, buf, "0123456789")
        if entered and buf.isdigit():
            g = int(buf)
            buf = ""
            if g == code:
                result = True
            else:
                log.append(f"{g:>2}  ->  {'HIGHER' if g < code else 'LOWER'}")
                if len(log) >= tries:
                    result = False
        if now - t0 > limit:
            result = False
        left = limit - (now - t0)
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 1, 2, "CRACK THE SUPPLY LOCKER", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
        timer_bar(scr, 2, 2, left, limit)
        steps = int((1 - left / limit) * 30)
        put(scr, 4, 4, "Footsteps: " + "." * (30 - steps) + "Z" * min(3, steps // 10 + 1), C(2))
        put(scr, 6, 4, "+-------+")
        put(scr, 7, 4, "| [ ? ] |   Guesses left: " + str(tries - len(log)))
        put(scr, 8, 4, "+-------+")
        for i, line in enumerate(log):
            put(scr, 10 + i, 6, line, C(3))
        put(scr, 11 + tries, 4, f"Your guess: {buf}_", curses.A_BOLD)
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.03)
    outro(scr, result, f"The code was {code}.")
    return result, {}


# ======================================================================
# 8. DECODE THE RADIO (live static + countdown)
# ======================================================================
RADIO = {"HARD": (8, 0.35), "NORMAL": (12, 0.2), "EASY": (20, 0.1)}   # seconds per word, static amount
RADIO_WORDS = ["SAFE ZONE", "BRIDGE", "CONVOY", "SHELTER", "BLIZZARD", "GATES", "MEDIC", "RESCUE", "WATER", "SUPPLY"]


def live_radio(scr, tier):
    _setup(scr)
    limit, static = RADIO[tier]
    intro(scr, "Decode the Radio", tier, [
        "A rescue broadcast is breaking up with static.",
        "Unscramble each word, type it and press ENTER.",
        "Static (#) flickers over the letters, so watch closely!",
        f"2 words, {limit} seconds each."])
    for n, word in enumerate(random.sample(RADIO_WORDS, 2), 1):
        letters = list(word.replace(" ", ""))
        while "".join(letters) == word.replace(" ", ""):
            random.shuffle(letters)
        t0, buf, result, shown, last_flicker = time.monotonic(), "", None, letters[:], 0
        while result is None:
            now = time.monotonic()
            buf, entered = read_key_into(scr, buf, "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ ")
            if entered:
                result = buf.replace(" ", "") == word.replace(" ", "")
            elif now - t0 > limit:
                result = False
            if now - last_flicker > 0.4:
                last_flicker = now
                shown = [("#" if random.random() < static else ch) for ch in letters]
            scr.erase()
            put(scr, 1, 2, f"DECODE THE RADIO   Word {n}/2", curses.A_BOLD | C(4))
            timer_bar(scr, 2, 2, limit - (now - t0), limit)
            put(scr, 5, 4, "~~ kzzzt ~~ " + "  ".join(shown) + " ~~ kzzzt ~~", curses.A_BOLD | C(3))
            put(scr, 8, 4, f"Your answer: {buf}_", curses.A_BOLD)
            scr.refresh()
            time.sleep(0.03)
        scr.erase()
        put(scr, 8, 4, ("Got it! " if result else "Lost the signal! ") + f"The word was {word}.",
            curses.A_BOLD | (C(1) if result else C(2)))
        scr.refresh()
        time.sleep(1.1)
        flush(scr)
        if not result:
            outro(scr, False)
            return False, {}
    outro(scr, True)
    return True, {}


# ======================================================================
# TEXT VERSIONS (backup when curses can't run)
# ======================================================================
def _timed(prompt):
    t = time.monotonic()
    a = input(prompt)
    return a.strip().upper(), time.monotonic() - t


TEXT_TIME = {   # seconds for the text versions
    "HARD": {"react": 1.0, "show": 2.0, "word": 2.5, "item": 3.0, "radio": 8.0, "lane": 2.0},
    "NORMAL": {"react": 1.6, "show": 3.5, "word": 4.0, "item": 5.0, "radio": 12.0, "lane": 3.0},
    "EASY": {"react": 2.5, "show": 6.0, "word": 7.0, "item": 8.0, "radio": 20.0, "lane": 5.0},
}


def text_lock_door(tier):
    window, wins = TEXT_TIME[tier]["react"], 0
    print(f"Press ENTER the moment you see LOCK! 3 rounds, win 2. ({window}s to react)")
    for rnd in range(1, 4):
        input(f"Round {rnd}: press ENTER to get ready...")
        time.sleep(random.uniform(1.5, 4))
        print("   >>> LOCK! <<<")
        _, took = _timed("")
        ok = 0.08 < took <= window
        print(f"   {'Locked' if ok else 'Missed'} ({took:.2f}s)")
        wins += ok
    return wins >= 2, {}


def text_escape(tier):
    show = TEXT_TIME[tier]["show"]
    for length in (4, 5):
        route = [random.choice(["LEFT", "RIGHT", "UP", "DOWN"]) for _ in range(length)]
        print(f"Memorize the escape route ({show}s):  " + " > ".join(route))
        time.sleep(show)
        print("\n" * 40)
        ans, _ = _timed("Type it back (like L U U R): ")
        if [c for c in ans if c in "LRUD"] != [m[0] for m in route]:
            print("   Wrong turn!")
            return False, {}
    return True, {}


def text_dodge(tier):
    limit, lives, hits = TEXT_TIME[tier]["lane"], {"HARD": 1, "NORMAL": 2, "EASY": 3}[tier], 0
    print(f"Wrecks ahead! Type the SAFE lane (L, M or R) within {limit}s. 5 rounds.")
    for _ in range(5):
        safe = random.choice("LMR")
        lanes = "  ".join("..." if l == safe else "###" for l in "LMR")
        ans, took = _timed(f"   L    M    R\n   {lanes}\n   Lane: ")
        if ans != safe or took > limit:
            hits += 1
            print("   CRASH!")
            if hits >= lives:
                return False, {}
    return True, {}


def text_barricade(tier):
    limit = TEXT_TIME[tier]["word"]
    for w in random.sample(WORDS, 3):
        ans, took = _timed(f"Type {w} ({limit}s): ")
        if ans != w or took > limit:
            return False, {}
    return True, {}


def text_safe_unsafe(tier):
    limit, right = TEXT_TIME[tier]["item"], 0
    print(f"SAFE or UNSAFE? Type S or U ({limit}s each). Get 4 of 5.")
    for text, truth in random.sample(SAFE_UNSAFE, 5):
        ans, took = _timed(f"   {text}: ")
        right += ans == truth and took <= limit
    return right >= 4, {}


def text_count(tier):
    show = TEXT_TIME[tier]["show"]
    count = random.randint(6, 16)
    cells = ["Z"] * count + ["."] * (60 - count)
    random.shuffle(cells)
    print(f"Count the Z ({show}s):")
    for r in range(5):
        print("   " + " ".join(cells[r * 12:(r + 1) * 12]))
    time.sleep(show)
    print("\n" * 40)
    ans, _ = _timed("How many? ")
    return ans.isdigit() and abs(int(ans) - count) <= 2, {}


def text_locker(tier):
    tries, limit = LOCKER[tier]
    code, t0 = random.randint(1, 20), time.monotonic()
    print(f"Locker code 1-20. {tries} guesses, {limit}s.")
    for left in range(tries, 0, -1):
        ans, _ = _timed(f"   Guess ({left} left): ")
        if time.monotonic() - t0 > limit:
            return False, {}
        if ans.isdigit() and int(ans) == code:
            return True, {}
        print("   HIGHER" if ans.isdigit() and int(ans) < code else "   LOWER")
    return False, {}


def text_radio(tier):
    limit = TEXT_TIME[tier]["radio"]
    for w in random.sample(RADIO_WORDS, 2):
        letters = list(w.replace(" ", ""))
        random.shuffle(letters)
        ans, took = _timed(f"Unscramble {''.join(letters)} ({limit}s): ")
        if ans.replace(" ", "") != w.replace(" ", "") or took > limit:
            return False, {}
    return True, {}


# ======================================================================
# Registry and the one function the engine calls
# ======================================================================
GAMES = {
    # name: (live version, text version, reward type)
    "Lock the Door": (live_lock_door, text_lock_door, "health"),
    "Escape the Horde": (live_escape_horde, text_escape, "health"),
    "Dodge the Wrecks": (live_dodge, text_dodge, "water"),
    "Barricade the Door": (live_barricade, text_barricade, "health"),
    "Safe or Unsafe?": (live_safe_unsafe, text_safe_unsafe, "food and water"),
    "Count the Infected": (live_count, text_count, "food"),
    "Crack the Supply Locker": (live_locker, text_locker, "food"),
    "Decode the Radio": (live_radio, text_radio, "water"),
}


def play(name, tier):
    """Run one mini game. Tries the live version first, then the text version."""
    live, text, _ = GAMES[name]
    if curses is not None and sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty():
        try:
            return curses.wrapper(live, tier)
        except TooSmall:
            print("(Make your terminal window bigger, at least 64 x 22, for the live version.)")
        except curses.error:
            pass
    print(f"\nMINI GAME ({tier}): {name}  [text version]")
    return text(tier)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Try any game directly:  python minigames.py "Dodge the Wrecks" HARD
    name = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else random.choice(list(GAMES))
    tier = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "NORMAL"
    print(play(name, tier))

================================================================================
FILE: play.py

"""
Zombie Escape - console version.

  python play.py                 play (pick a city)
  python play.py --city NYC --seed 42 --debug   show every probability calculation
  python play.py --auto balanced  let an AI policy play (balanced, lowest_risk, supplies, speed, random, best_rating)
"""
import argparse
import random
import sys
import time

from zombie_sim.engine import Game, load_fallbacks, ENDINGS
from zombie_sim.data_loader import load_world
import os
from zombie_sim.attributes import load_attributes, load_content, CONTENT
from zombie_sim.policies import POLICIES
from zombie_sim.params import PARAMS

TIME_LIMIT = PARAMS["timer_seconds"]


def bar(v, width=20):
    n = int(round(max(0, min(100, v)) / 100 * width))
    return "#" * n + "." * (width - n)


class ConsoleUI:
    def __init__(self, debug=False, policy=None):
        self.debug, self.policy = debug, policy

    def status(self, g):
        S, E, I, R = g.local()
        st = g.stops[g.place["a"]]
        c = g.counties[st["geoid"]]
        print(f"  {g.fmt_hour(g.hour)} | {g.place_label()} | {g.total_mi - g.miles:,.0f} mi to go | deadline Day 7 24:00")
        print(f"  HEALTH {g.health:5.1f} {bar(g.health)}  FOOD {g.food:5.1f}  WATER {g.water:5.1f}  "
              f"FUEL {g.fuel:4.1f} gal  {'vehicle' if g.vehicle else 'ON FOOT'}")
        print(f"  Outbreak in {c['name']}, {c['state']}: {I * 100:.1f}% infectious, {E * 100:.1f}% exposed "
              f"\n  January normal at this stop (NOAA 1991-2020): {g.weather()[0]:.1f}F - story weather may be a fictional storm"
              f"\n  (R0 {g.traj[g.place['a']].r0(g.outbreak_day()):.1f}, Re {g.traj[g.place['a']].r_effective(g.outbreak_day()):.1f}; fictional)")

    def choose(self, g, scene, options, kind):
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        label = {"main": f"Day {scene.get('day')} {scene.get('time')}", "callback": "CALLBACK",
                 "detour": "DETOUR", "fallback": "ON THE ROAD", "event": "EVENT"}[kind]
        print(f"{label}: {scene['title']}")
        self.status(g)
        print("\n" + scene["text"])
        for o in options:
            tag = {"low_fuel": " [low fuel]", "infected_symptoms": " [symptoms]", "behind": " [behind schedule]",
                   "low_health": " [low health]"}.get(o.get("condition"), "")
            if o.get("unlock_flag"):
                tag = f" [unlocked: {o['unlock_flag']}]"
            print(f"  {o['letter']}. {o['text']}{tag}")
        if self.policy:
            return self.policy(g, scene, options)
        t0 = time.time()
        choice = input(f"Choose {'/'.join(o['letter'] for o in options)}" + ("" if self.debug else f" ({TIME_LIMIT} seconds)") + ": ").strip().upper()
        letters = [o["letter"] for o in options]
        if (not self.debug and time.time() - t0 > TIME_LIMIT) or choice not in letters:
            choice = random.choice(letters)
            print(f"  Too slow or unclear. You froze, and your feet chose {choice}.")
        return choice

    def outcome(self, g, scene, o, r):
        inj, inf, a = r["injury"], r["infection"], r["attrs"]
        print(f"  -> {o['note']}")
        for m in r["msgs"]:
            print("  * " + m["text"])
        if self.debug:
            snow = "no NOAA snow normal" if inj["snow_in"] is None else f"{inj['snow_in']:.1f} in snow"
            print(f"  [injury]   {inj['base']:.2f} base x {inj['weather']:.2f} weather ({inj['temp_f']:.1f}F, {snow}) "
                  f"x {inj['activity']:.2f} {a['activity']} x {inj['time']:.2f} time = {inj['p']:.1%}  roll {r['roll_injury']:.3f}")
            print(f"  [infection] 1-exp(-{inf['k']} k x {inf['prevalence']:.3f} prevalence x {inf['hours']}h x "
                  f"{inf['setting']} {a['setting']} x {inf['night']} night x {inf['gear']} gear) = {inf['p']:.2%}  "
                  f"roll {r['roll_infection']:.3f}")
            print(f"  [rating {o['rating']}] time {a['hours']}h, fuel {a['fuel_gal']:+g}, {a['evidence'] or 'no special effects'}")

    def minigame(self, g, name, tier):
        if self.policy:
            return None
        if name in g.rgames:
            return self.realistic(g.rgames[name], tier)
        print("\n" + "*" * 70 + f"\nMINI GAME ({tier}): {name}")
        try:
            import minigames
            return minigames.play(name, tier)
        except Exception as exc:   # report it: the engine then uses the simulated result
            print(f"  (live mini game unavailable: {exc}; result simulated)")
            return None

    def realistic(self, game, tier):
        """Console version of a realistic mini game: put the real steps in the right order before time runs out."""
        import re
        steps = [x.strip() for x in re.split(r"\s*\d+\.\s+", game["steps"]) if x.strip()]
        order = list(range(len(steps)))
        random.shuffle(order)
        limit = {"EASY": 90, "NORMAL": 60, "HARD": 40}[tier]
        print("\n" + "*" * 70 + f"\nMINI GAME ({tier}): {game['name']}")
        print(f"Goal: type the steps in the correct real-world order (e.g. 3 1 2 ...). You have {limit} seconds.")
        if tier == "EASY":
            print("Hint: " + game["mistakes"])
        for n, k in enumerate(order, 1):
            print(f"  {n}. {steps[k]}")
        t0 = time.time()
        ans = input("Your order: ").replace(",", " ").split()
        try:
            picked = [order[int(x) - 1] for x in ans]
        except (ValueError, IndexError):
            picked = []
        win = picked == list(range(len(steps))) and time.time() - t0 <= limit
        print("Good job! That's the right order." if win else "Not quite. The right order was: " + " -> ".join(steps))
        return (win, {})

    def message(self, g, title, msgs):
        print(f"\n-- {title} --")
        for m in msgs:
            print("  * " + m["text"])

    def end(self, g):
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print(f"ENDING: {g.ending} - {ENDINGS[g.ending]}" + (f" ({g.ending_detail})" if g.ending_detail else ""))
        s = g.summary()
        print(f"Time {g.fmt_hour(g.hour)}  health {g.health:.0f}  food {g.food:.0f}  water {g.water:.0f}  "
              f"fuel {g.fuel:.1f}  miles left {s['miles_left']:.0f}")
        print("Choices:", s["choices"], "| mini games:", s["minigames"])
        print("Supply ledger (gains / losses):")
        for k in ("health", "food", "water", "fuel"):
            gain = sum(l[k] for l in g.ledger if l[k] > 0)
            loss = sum(-l[k] for l in g.ledger if l[k] < 0)
            print(f"  {k:7} +{gain:6.1f}  -{loss:6.1f}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--city", choices=["NYC", "BOS", "PIT", "SLC", "JAC", "SEA", "AUS"])
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    ap.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--auto", choices=sorted(POLICIES))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    world, attrs, fb = load_world(), load_attributes(), load_fallbacks()
    content = load_content(os.path.join(CONTENT, "scenarios_v2.json"))
    city = args.city
    if not city:
        for i, c in enumerate(content["cities"], 1):
            print(f"{i}. {c['start']} -> {c['end']}")
        city = content["cities"][int(input("Pick a city 1-7: ")) - 1]["code"]
    seed = args.seed if args.seed is not None else random.randrange(1, 10 ** 9)
    print(f"Seed {seed} (replay this game with --seed {seed})")
    g = Game(world, content, attrs, fb, city, seed)
    g.run(ConsoleUI(args.debug, POLICIES.get(args.auto)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""
Self-hosted web server for Zombie Escape. Python standard library only, no domain needed.

  python server.py                    http://localhost:8000 (this computer only)
  python server.py --host 0.0.0.0     also reachable from other devices on your network at
                                      http://<this computer's IP address>:8000
  python server.py --port 9000

Endpoints:
  /                 the game (web/index.html)
  /health           "ok" (for uptime checks)
  /api/montecarlo?city=NYC&policy=balanced&runs=500    Monte Carlo from the Python engine (JSON)
"""
import argparse
import http.server
import json
import os
import socket
import sys
import threading
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
WEB = os.path.join(ROOT, "web")
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

LOCK = threading.Lock()


class Handler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *a, **kw):
        super().__init__(*a, directory=WEB, **kw)

    def end_headers(self):
        self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
        super().end_headers()

    def _json(self, code, obj):
        body = json.dumps(obj).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self):
        u = urlparse(self.path)
        if u.path == "/health":
            body = b"ok"
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", "2")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)
            return
        if u.path == "/api/montecarlo":
            from zombie_sim.sim import monte_carlo
            from zombie_sim.policies import POLICIES
            q = parse_qs(u.query)
            city = q.get("city", ["NYC"])[0].upper()
            pol = q.get("policy", ["balanced"])[0]
            try:
                runs = max(1, min(2000, int(q.get("runs", ["500"])[0])))
            except ValueError:
                return self._json(400, {"error": "runs must be a whole number"})
            if city not in ("NYC", "BOS", "PIT", "SLC", "JAC", "SEA", "AUS") or pol not in POLICIES:
                return self._json(400, {"error": "unknown city or policy", "policies": sorted(POLICIES)})
            with LOCK:
                res = monte_carlo(city, POLICIES[pol], runs)
            res.pop("rows", None)
            return self._json(200, {"city": city, "policy": pol, **res,
                                    "note": "Probabilities inside the game's fictional model, not real-world odds."})
        return super().do_GET()

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        sys.stderr.write("%s - %s\n" % (self.address_string(), fmt % args))


def lan_ip():
    try:
        s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        s.connect(("10.255.255.255", 1))
        ip = s.getsockname()[0]
        s.close()
        return ip
    except OSError:
        return None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("PORT", 8000)))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(WEB, "data.js")):
        sys.exit("web/data.js is missing. Run: python tools/build_web.py")
    srv = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer((a.host, a.port), Handler)
    print(f"Zombie Escape running at http://localhost:{a.port}")
    if a.host == "0.0.0.0" and lan_ip():
        print(f"Other devices on your network: http://{lan_ip()}:{a.port}")
    print("Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
    try:
        srv.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

FILE: data/data_sources.md

# Data sources

Every number in `city_data.csv`, `weather_data.csv` and `route_data.csv` was downloaded from the source named below (retrieved November 2026). Nothing in these three files was estimated or made up. Values the source did not publish are left **blank**, and the code treats a blank as missing, never as zero.

## city_data.csv: counties (44 rows)

| Column | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `geoid` | U.S. Census Bureau FIPS code | 2-digit state + 3-digit county |
| `county_name`, `state_name` | Census | |
| `geo_type` | | Always `county`. Every place in the game is a **county**, not a city proper. "New York City" uses New York County (Manhattan); "Boston" uses Suffolk County. |
| `pop_estimates_base_2020` | Census Vintage 2023 county population estimates, file `co-est2023-alldata.csv`, column `ESTIMATESBASE2020` | https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2023/counties/totals/ |
| `pop_estimate_2023` | Same file, column `POPESTIMATE2023` (July 1, 2023) | Used by the game |
| `land_area_sq_m` | Census TIGERweb, `State_County` MapServer layer 1, field `AREALAND` (square meters) | https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1 |
| `internal_point_lat`, `internal_point_lon` | Same TIGERweb layer, `CENTLAT` / `CENTLON` | Census "internal point", not a city center |

**Transformation (done in code, `zombie_sim/data_loader.py`):** land area in sq mi = `AREALAND / 2,589,988.11`; density = `POPESTIMATE2023 / land sq mi`. Density is never stored, always calculated.

## weather_data.csv: NOAA stations (42 rows)

| Column | Source |
|---|---|
| `station_id`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `elevation_m` | NOAA NCEI station metadata returned with the normals |
| `jan_tavg_normal_f` | NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, `MLY-TAVG-NORMAL`, January (°F) |
| `jan_prcp_normal_in` | Same, `MLY-PRCP-NORMAL`, January (inches) |
| `jan_snow_normal_in` | Same, `MLY-SNOW-NORMAL`, January (inches). **Blank** for Poughkeepsie (USW00014757), Laramie (USW00024022) and Denver (USW00003017; not used on a route) because NOAA publishes no snowfall normal for them. |

API used: `https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1?dataset=normals-monthly-1991-2020&stations=...&dataTypes=MLY-TAVG-NORMAL,MLY-PRCP-NORMAL,MLY-SNOW-NORMAL&format=csv`

These are **long-term January averages**, not the weather on any real day. Several scenarios describe fictional storms (for example "-12°F in Laramie"). The game uses the normal for its math and labels the story weather as fiction.

**Station choice:** the main airport or long-record station nearest each route stop. Distance from the county internal point is calculated in code (`station_distance_mi`). Three stops have no first-order station in the county and use the nearest one with complete normals:

| Stop | Station | Distance |
|---|---|---|
| Guadalupe County, NM (BOS day 7) | Albuquerque airport | about 104 mi |
| Emery County, UT (PIT day 6) | Grand Junction airport, CO | about 116 mi |
| Rockingham County, VA (AUS day 4) | Washington Dulles airport | about 82 mi |

Rejected during collection: USW00094012 (turned out to be Havre, MT, from its returned coordinates); USW00014714 and USW00023063 (no normals returned).

## route_data.csv: route stops (7 routes × 8 stops)

| Column | Source |
|---|---|
| `stop_day`, `stop_label` | The game's story (stop 1 = start city, stops 2–7 = each day's morning location, stop 8 = safe zone) |
| `county_geoid`, `station_id` | Links to the two files above |
| `waypoint_lat`, `waypoint_lon` | The NOAA station coordinates, or the Census county internal point when `waypoint_source = county_internal_point` |
| `leg_to_next_m`, `leg_to_next_s` | Driving distance (meters) and free-flow duration (seconds) to the next stop from the OSRM routing engine on OpenStreetMap data: `https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1/driving/lon,lat;lon,lat;...`. The duration is stored for reference only; the game calculates its own winter speed. |

**Transformation:** miles = meters / 1,609.344; cumulative miles summed in code. Route totals: NYC 2,249, BOS 2,404, PIT 2,249, SLC 2,230, JAC 2,416, SEA 2,412, AUS 2,296 road miles.

OpenStreetMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.

## svi_data.csv (added in version 2)

| Column | Source |
|---|---|
| `geoid` | Census county FIPS, the 44 route counties |
| `svi_overall` | CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022, county `RPL_THEMES` (0 = least, 1 = most vulnerable) |
| `pct_age65` | SVI 2022 `EP_AGE65` (ACS 2018–2022 estimate of % aged 65+) |
| `pct_no_vehicle` | SVI 2022 `EP_NOVEH` (% of households with no vehicle) |
| `source`, `retrieved` | CDC SVI 2022 ArcGIS county layer (`.../CDC_ATSDR_Social_Vulnerability_Index_2022_USA/FeatureServer`, layer 1), retrieved 2026-11-19 |

**Use in the game:** SVI only changes evacuation difficulty: the SVI event (SVI ≥ 0.75) and a congestion delay of 2 + 6 × SVI hours on some options. It never changes infection or survival chance directly. % aged 65+ scales the fictional zombie's spread rate by ±1% per point from the route mean (clamped 0.9–1.1); this is a FICTIONAL rule using a REAL input.

## r0_reference.csv and rabies_reference.csv

Published values entered by hand with citations (Guerra et al. 2017; Biggerstaff et al. 2014; Liu et al. 2020; Liu & Rocklöv 2021; Hampson et al. 2009; CDC MMWR 2008 and 2010). Used for the R0 event text and the end-screen comparison table, and the rabies event. No game probability is computed from them.

## Not included (and why)

| Dataset | Status | How to add it |
|---|---|---|
| OpenStreetMap hospitals, grocery stores, fuel stations near each stop | **Not collected.** The Overpass API was not reachable from the build environment. The game does **not** pretend to know these; fuel found in town is a labeled fictional rule. | Query Overpass (`https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`) with e.g. `[out:json];(node["amenity"="fuel"](around:16000,LAT,LON););out count;` for each stop and save `poi_data.csv` with columns `county_geoid, amenity, count_within_10mi, query_date`. Then replace `town_fuel_min/max` in `params.py` with a rule based on the count. |
| Real outbreak data | Not applicable | The zombie is fictional. Spread rates are invented and labeled as such. |

## Replacing a dataset

1. Edit or replace the CSV (keep the column names).
2. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_data.py`. The loader reports every invalid or missing value by file and line.
3. Run `python tools/build_web.py` to rebuild the web game's data bundle.

FILE: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# Architecture

```
data/                 REAL data (CSV) + data_sources.md
content/              the story: scenarios_v2.json (revised scenes, events, realistic mini games; built by
                      tools/build_content_v2.py), scenarios.json (v1), fallbacks.json,
                      option_attributes.csv (time/fuel/exposure per option, editable)
zombie_sim/           the simulation (no screen code)
  params.py           every FICTIONAL coefficient in one place
  data_loader.py      reads + validates the CSVs, calculates density and road miles
  seir.py             SEIR curves (RK4), R0, effective R, sensitivity
  rng.py              seeded Mulberry32 + named streams (same as JS)
  attributes.py       reads option text -> option_attributes.csv
  engine.py           game rules: clock, travel, fuel, injury, infection, rolls, endings, ledger
  policies.py         AI strategies for Monte Carlo
  sim.py              headless runs + Monte Carlo summary
play.py               console game (uses minigames.py for live curses mini games)
server.py             self-hosted web server (standard library only)
web/                  browser game
  sim.js              JavaScript port of zombie_sim (parity-tested)
  game.js             screens, status dashboard, pause, units, developer mode, charts, 8 canvas mini games
  realgames.js        the 10 realistic step-by-step mini games
  data.js             generated bundle (tools/build_web.py)
tools/                build_attributes.py, build_web.py, monte_carlo_report.py
tests/                pytest suite, Python-vs-JS parity, server, browser playthrough
reports/              survival report, charts, CSVs, screenshots
```

## Flow of one game

```
load_world() ──> Census/NOAA/OSRM CSVs ──> counties (density), stations, routes (cumulative miles)
Game(seed)   ──> outbreak strength ──> one SEIR Trajectory per route stop
run(ui):
  for each of 14 story scenes:
    travel_to(scene)      drive: speed from weather, fuel from mpg, road-accident roll
                          no fuel / no vehicle -> fallback scene (max 3, then STRANDED)
                          Morning stops: town fuel; early -> rest until scheduled time
    deadline check        -> TOO_LATE
    real-data event       one per scene if due: rabies, fuel, R0, SVI, age (engine.event_due)
    due callbacks         (flag + delay, unchanged)
    ask(scene)            ui.choose -> resolve():
                            injury roll   (base x weather x activity x time)
                            infection roll (1 - exp(-k p t M)), hidden timer
                            supplies, fuel, vehicle, miles, medicine, flags
                            advance clock -> food/water drain, starvation, infection onset
    every 2 scenes        pair roll -> mini game or detour (no repeats)
  arrive()                distance + deadline + gate screening -> ending
```

The engine never draws anything. It calls four methods on a `ui` object (`choose`, `outcome`, `minigame`, `message`, plus `end`). The console, the browser and the Monte Carlo simulator are three different `ui` objects driving the same rules.

## Python and JavaScript

The Python package is the reference. `web/sim.js` repeats it line by line, using the same random generator and the same order of random draws. `tests/test_parity.py` plays 210 games (7 routes × 5 seeds × 6 strategies) in both languages and requires identical choices, endings and mini games, and equal numbers to 1e-9.

## Changing things

| To change… | Edit | Then |
|---|---|---|
| a coefficient | `zombie_sim/params.py` | `python tools/build_web.py`, run tests |
| a dataset | `data/*.csv` | tests, `build_web.py` |
| an option's time/fuel/exposure | `content/option_attributes.csv` | `build_web.py` |
| story text | `content/scenarios.json` | `build_attributes.py` (overwrites hand edits), `build_web.py` |

## Version 2 option fields

Options in `scenarios_v2.json` carry their attributes inline and may add: `unlock_flag` (shown only after an earlier choice), `condition` (low_fuel, infected_symptoms, behind, low_health), `harm` ({health, reason}), `treat` (90% cure), `medicine_chance`, `svi_delay`, `gate` (final-gate quarantine or fuel), `sets_flags`, `minigame` (a story-linked realistic game) and `weather_rating`. Every health loss goes through `engine.hurt(amount, source, why)`, so the screen can always say why.

# Phase 1 audit: the game before this refactor

## What existed

| Part | File(s) | What it did |
|---|---|---|
| Console game | `zombie_game_engine.py` | 14 main scenarios per city (7 days × morning/night), timed input, injury rolls, exposure timer, food/water drain per scenario, roll every 2 picks, detours, callbacks, ledger |
| Outbreak model | `outbreak_model.py` | SEIR per route day, Euler method, 24 steps per day |
| Mini games | `minigames.py` (console, curses) and `web/game.js` (browser canvas) | 8 games, 3 tiers, no repeats in a playthrough |
| Content | `zombie_game_data.json` built from text files | 7 cities × (14 main + 4 detours + 2 callbacks) = 140 scenes, 560 options |
| Route "data" | `route_data.csv` | Density and January temperature for 49 route days |
| Web game | `web/engine.js`, `web/game.js`, `web/index.html` | A separate JavaScript copy of the rules |

## Hardcoded vs calculated (before)

| Value | Before |
|---|---|
| Density and temperature per route day | **Hardcoded approximations** typed into `route_data.csv`, not downloaded and not sourced |
| Route miles | Hardcoded round numbers in the story |
| Infection % in the story text and profiles | Some hardcoded in text; the model calculated the rest |
| Injury chances | Hidden per-option values in rating bands (kept) |
| Exposure chance | Calculated, but only after an injury: injury and infection were one event |

## Problems found

1. **Negative transmission.** The cold multiplier `(1 + 0.01·(50 − T)) × (1 − 0.03·(20 − T))` goes below zero under about −13°F, so the outbreak would run backwards.
2. **Victory ignored travel.** Surviving scenario 14 counted as reaching the safe zone. Time, distance and fuel did not exist.
3. **Injury and infection were the same roll.** Infection could only happen after an injury on a RISKY/WORST pick, and zombies nearby also raised the injury chance. The two risks were double counted.
4. **Data was not real.** Densities and temperatures were reasonable guesses with no source.
5. **Two copies of the rules** (Python and JavaScript) with nothing checking that they agreed.
6. **Python `random` and JS `Math.random`**: games could not be replayed or compared.
7. **Euler steps** with no check that S+E+I+R stayed equal to the population.
8. **No test suite** beyond manual playthroughs.

## What changed (summary)

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Negative transmission | Cold "stiffening" now has a floor of 0.40; tested from −60°F to 80°F |
| Victory | Requires: alive, not turned, physically at the safe zone (road miles), before Day 7 midnight. Five other endings. |
| Injury vs infection | Two separate formulas, rolls and random streams |
| Data | Census, TIGERweb, NOAA normals and OSRM distances downloaded and documented in `data/data_sources.md` |
| Two copies | `web/sim.js` is a port of `zombie_sim/`; `tests/test_parity.py` runs 210 games in both and checks every choice and number |
| Randomness | Seeded Mulberry32 generator with named streams, identical in both languages |
| SEIR | 4th-order Runge–Kutta, 1-hour steps, clamped and renormalized, conservation tested |
| Tests | 62 automated tests plus a headless-browser playthrough of all 7 routes |

## Preserved

All 7 cities, 140 scenes, 560 options and their text, the hidden ratings and injury values, all callbacks and flags, the 4 detours per city, the roll every 2 picks, all 8 mini games with their controls, tiers, rewards and the no-repeat rule.

FILE: docs/MATH.md

# The math, labeled

Every quantity is one of four kinds:

- **REAL**: downloaded data (see `data/data_sources.md`)
- **FICTIONAL**: an invented game assumption (all in `zombie_sim/params.py`)
- **CALCULATED**: computed from the two above
- **DECISION**: comes from the player's choices and the story text

## 1. Places

| Quantity | Kind | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| Population | REAL | Census 2023 estimate (county) |
| Land area | REAL | TIGERweb AREALAND / 2,589,988.11 |
| Density *d* | CALCULATED | population / land sq mi |
| January temperature *T*, snowfall | REAL | NOAA 1991–2020 normals at the nearest station |
| Road distance | REAL | OSRM on OpenStreetMap |

## 2. Outbreak (SEIR), one independent curve per county

```
dS/dt = −β(t)·S·I
dE/dt =  β(t)·S·I − σ·E
dI/dt =  σ·E − γ·I
dR/dt =  γ·I            (S, E, I, R are shares of the county population; they sum to 1)
```

| Symbol | Value | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| β base | 1.5 per day | FICTIONAL |
| σ = 1 / incubation | 1 / 1 day | FICTIONAL |
| γ | 0.15 per day | FICTIONAL |
| Initial infectious | 0.001% | FICTIONAL |
| Game Day 1 08:00 | outbreak day 7.0 | FICTIONAL |
| Density multiplier | clamp(1 + 0.2·log10(d/100), 0.6, 1.8) | FICTIONAL rule on REAL density |
| Cold multiplier | (1 + 0.01·max(0, 50 − T)) × max(0.40, 1 − 0.03·(20 − T)) when T < 20 | FICTIONAL rule on REAL temperature |
| Winter ramp | × (1 + 0.02·t) | FICTIONAL |
| Outbreak strength | each playthrough × U(0.9, 1.1) | FICTIONAL (seeded) |

β(t) = 1.5 × density mult × cold mult × (1 + 0.02t) × strength.

**Solver:** 4th-order Runge–Kutta, 1-hour steps over 16 days. After each step tiny negative rounding errors are set to 0 and the shares renormalized. Tested: all shares ≥ 0, sum = 1 to 12 decimal places, results unchanged (to 0.0001) with 15-minute steps. The curve is always calculated, never typed in.

**R0 and effective R** (CALCULATED from fictional parameters): R0(t) = β(t)/γ; R_eff(t) = R0(t)·S(t). With the default parameters, R0 at the start counties ranges from about 10 (Teton County, WY, 6 people/sq mi, 16°F) to 21 (Manhattan). These describe the invented zombie, not any real disease.

**Limitation:** counties do not exchange infected people. Each stop's curve is its own. A halfway point between two stops averages their curves.

**Sensitivity** (`reports/seir_sensitivity.csv`): with β from 1.0 to 2.0 and γ from 0.10 to 0.30, Day 4 prevalence at the most infected stop ranges from about 3% to over 70%. Higher β or lower γ always means more infection. Balanced-strategy survival with β = 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 is in the survival report.

## 3. Injury risk (separate from infection)

```
P(injury) = min(0.95, base × weather × activity × time)
```

| Factor | Value | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| base | the option's hidden injury chance (BEST 0–10%, OKAY 10–25%, RISKY 30–55%, WORST 60–85%) | FICTIONAL (existing game) |
| weather | outdoor (`open`) options only: min(1.5, 1 + 0.01·max(0, 32 − T) + 0.01·snow). If NOAA has no snow normal, the snow term is skipped and the screen says so. Indoors / in a vehicle: 1.0 | FICTIONAL rule on REAL normals |
| activity | travel 1.0, scavenge 1.0, contact 1.1, social 0.85, shelter 0.75 | FICTIONAL |
| time | 1.15 at night | FICTIONAL |

The damage is the option's existing hidden damage value. The local outbreak does **not** change injury risk.

## 4. Infection risk

```
P(infection) = 1 − exp(−k × p × t × M)
M = setting × night × gear
```

| Factor | Value | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| k by exposure | none 0, low 0.05, medium 0.2, high 0.5, contact 1.5 | FICTIONAL |
| p | infectious share I where the player is, at that hour | CALCULATED (SEIR) |
| t | hours the option takes | DECISION (from the option text) |
| setting | vehicle 0.3, shelter 0.5, open 1.0 | FICTIONAL |
| night | 1.25 | FICTIONAL |
| gear | 1.0 (no protective-gear item exists in the story yet) | FICTIONAL |

Each factor appears once, so nothing is counted twice. Infection is hidden. Symptoms appear 24 hours later; the player **turns** at 36 hours unless treated. Medicine (found in the story) cures 90% of the time before onset. Arriving infected but not yet turned means quarantine at the safe zone, with the same 90% cure chance.

## 5. Time, travel and fuel

| Rule | Value | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| Clock | Day 1 08:00 = hour 0; deadline Day 7 24:00 = hour 160 | FICTIONAL |
| Story stops | Morning of day *d* at stop *d*; Night halfway to stop *d+1*; Day 7 Night at the safe zone | FICTIONAL layout on REAL road miles |
| Speed | 50 mph / (1 + 0.005·max(0, 32 − T) + 0.02·snow), × 0.85 overnight | FICTIONAL rule on REAL normals |
| Fuel | 25 mpg, 25-gallon tank, starts full | FICTIONAL |
| Fuel in towns | each Morning stop: U(8, 16) gallons | FICTIONAL (OSM fuel-station data not collected) |
| Road accident | 1 − exp(−0.01 × cold factor × driving hours), −8 health | FICTIONAL |
| Arriving early | the player rests until the scene's scheduled time | rule |
| Option time, fuel, vehicle, extra miles | read from each option's own text and note (`content/option_attributes.csv`, with the matching phrase in the `evidence` column) | DECISION |

No fuel or no vehicle means the player cannot drive. A **fallback scene** plays (Running on Fumes / On Foot). After 3 fallback scenes on the same leg the player is **stranded**.

## 6. Food, water, health

Food drains 8 and water 10 per 12 hours (the old "per scenario" rule, now tied to the clock). At 0 food the player loses 8 health per 12 hours; at 0 water, 12. All resources are clamped to 0–100 (fuel to 0–25 gal) and every change goes into the ledger with its cause.

## 7. Rolls and mini games (unchanged)

Every 2 main picks: risky pair → 0–60 HARD mini game, 61–100 detour; mixed pair → 0–50 NORMAL, else EASY; good pair → EASY, double reward above 50. HARD win +5 health, loss −20 to −30; NORMAL win +15 of the reward type, loss −10 to −15; EASY win +25 (×2 on the double roll), loss free. The 8 mini games never repeat in one playthrough. In simulations, mini games are won with fixed chances (35% / 60% / 85%).

## 8. Endings

| Ending | Condition |
|---|---|
| VICTORY | alive, not turned (or cured), at the safe zone's road mile, by hour 160 |
| DIED | health 0 |
| TURNED | untreated infection reached onset, or the gate treatment failed |
| TOO_LATE | the clock passed Day 7 midnight |
| STRANDED | out of fuel/vehicle after 3 fallback scenes, or not at the safe zone when the story ended |
| DENIED | the final option says the gate turned the player away |

## 9. Random numbers

Mulberry32, seeded per game. Each kind of random event has its own named stream (outbreak, injury, infection, road, town_fuel, treat, roll, minigame_pick, minigame_win, minigame_dmg, policy). The same seed with the same choices replays the same game. Monte Carlo runs every strategy on seeds 1–N, so the strategies face matched random numbers for the same kind of event.

## 10. What the survival percentages mean

They are frequencies inside this model. They show how the game's rules reward or punish strategies. They are **not** estimates of anyone's real chance of surviving anything.

## 11. Version 2 additions

| Rule | Formula | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Age multiplier on β | `clamp(1 + 0.01 × (pct65 − 16.08), 0.9, 1.1)`; 16.08 = mean % aged 65+ across the 44 route counties | REAL input (SVI 2022 EP_AGE65), FICTIONAL rule |
| SVI congestion delay | `factor × (2 + 6 × SVI)` hours on options with `svi_delay` | REAL input (SVI 2022 RPL_THEMES), FICTIONAL rule |
| Events | rabies (infected, not yet symptomatic, no cure item) → fuel (< 8 gal, Morning) → R0 (Day 3 Night) → SVI ≥ 0.75 → % 65+ ≥ 20; at most one per scene, each once | DECISION |
| Treatment options | 90% cure if infected and untreated (`treatment_success`) | FICTIONAL |
| Symptom list flag | symptoms warn 6 h earlier | FICTIONAL |
| Fixed costs (`harm`) | flat health loss with a stated reason | FICTIONAL |
| Final gate | quarantine hours are not counted against the deadline; fuel gates need a stated number of gallons or add hours | DECISION |
| Realistic mini games | follow real steps; fixed win/fail effects per game; no loss on EASY; cold hands = controls slowed by `clamp((32 − °F)/50, 0, 0.5)` from the NOAA normal; mistake noise × (1 + 3 × local infectious share); boiling rule 1 min, 3 min above 6,500 ft (CDC) from station elevation | REAL inputs, FICTIONAL scoring |

## 12. Monte Carlo, version 2 (1,000 runs per route per strategy, seeds 1–1000)

| Strategy | Survival | Main failure |
|---|---|---|
| Balanced | 96.9% | turned 2.5% |
| Lowest risk | 96.9% | turned 2.1% |
| Always BEST | 94.6% | turned 3.2% |
| Max supplies | 37.9% | too late 57.4% |
| Max speed | 14.3% | died 84.9% |
| Random | 11.5% | died 67.1% |

Careful play survives about 97% of the time, because infection is now usually curable (treatment options, the rabies event, the wound check). Full tables: `reports/survival_report.md`.

## 13. Version 3: arrival seeding (replaces the single 0.001% start)

Every county used to start at 0.001% infectious, so the first days were nearly risk-free and tiny rural counties stayed safe all week, while big cities neared their peak. Version 3 gives each route stop its own starting level (`i0`), solved so that, at the player's scheduled arrival and with outbreak strength 1.0, the county is near a target:

| Step | Rule | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Arrival time | stop k (0–6) = Day k+1 08:00; safe zone = Day 7 20:00 | DECISION |
| Base target | 5% on Day 1, rising in a straight line to 35% at the Day 7 evening arrival | FICTIONAL |
| Density tilt | + 10 points × clamp(log10(density / 100) / 2, −1, 1): 1/sq mi → −10, 100 → 0, 10,000+ → +10 | REAL input, FICTIONAL rule |
| Limits | target between 2% and 60% | FICTIONAL |
| Solve | log-spaced scan of starting levels, then 30 bisection steps (`seir.calibrate_i0`) | CALCULATED |

Story framing: the outbreak reached each county at a different time. The game's random outbreak strength (±10%) still moves each run above or below the target, and the curve keeps growing after you arrive, so arriving late is still more dangerous.

Monte Carlo, 1,000 runs per route per strategy:

| Strategy | v2 survival | v3 survival | v2 infected | v3 infected | v3 turned |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Balanced | 96.9% | 96.0% | 27.3% | 37.6% | 3.4% |
| Lowest risk | 96.9% | 95.7% | 26.0% | 31.9% | 3.3% |
| Always BEST | 94.6% | 93.6% | 36.4% | 46.0% | 4.7% |
| Random | 11.5% | 9.8% | 34.9% | 51.9% | 19.3% |

Infections are now more common, and careless play turns almost twice as often. Careful play still survives about 96%, because infection is usually caught and cured (90% treatments, the rabies event, the wound check, the gate screening). The next lever for difficulty is the cure side, not the outbreak.

================================================================================
FILE: docs/PRESENTATION.md

# Presenting Zombie Escape (talking points)

**1. What it is.** A choose-your-own-adventure escape across the U.S. in January. Seven start cities, 14 story stops, 20 seconds per choice, 8 mini games. The game runs in a browser or in the console.

**2. What is real.** Every place is a real county. The game uses the Census Bureau's 2023 population estimates and land area to calculate density (Manhattan: about 70,500 people per square mile; Teton County, Wyoming: about 2). Temperatures and snowfall are NOAA's official 1991–2020 January averages. Distances are real driving distances from OpenStreetMap (about 2,200–2,400 miles per route).

**3. What is invented, and labeled.** The zombie, how fast it spreads, and every risk number. The game marks them in orange on screen, keeps them all in one file (`params.py`) and lists them in `docs/MATH.md`.

**4. How the outbreak works.** An SEIR model. People go from Susceptible to Exposed to Infectious to Removed. Crowded and cold places spread faster (people crowd indoors), but very cold places slow the zombies down. Each county has its own curve. In the game you can watch your county's curve with a "you are here" line.

**5. Two separate risks.** Getting hurt depends on the choice, the weather and the dark. Getting infected depends on how many infected are around you, how long you're exposed and whether you're in a car or out in the open. After every choice the game shows the full calculation.

**6. Trade-offs.** Supplies cost time. Time matters because the safe zone seals at midnight on Day 7. Driving burns fuel; running out means a roadside scene. A detour can save a day or lose one.

**7. Monte Carlo.** We let six computer strategies play each route 1,000 times with the same random numbers. Careful strategies survive about 80–84% of the time, "speed first" about 69%, and random choices about 11%. At the end of each game, the page runs 500 trips in *your* style and compares.

**8. Testing.** 62 automated tests: the data loads and rejects bad values, the outbreak never goes negative and always adds up to the population, the rules work (no driving without fuel, no win without arriving), the browser version gives exactly the same results as the Python version, and the server works.

**9. Honest limits.** Counties don't infect each other. Fuel found in towns is a game rule, not real gas-station data. The survival percentages are game odds, not real-world odds.

Charts for slides: `reports/survival_by_policy.png`, `reports/endings_by_policy.png`, `reports/survival_by_route.png`, `reports/seir_start_counties.png`, screenshots in `reports/screenshots/`.

# Scenario revisions (Word doc only)

These files produce `docs/word/Zombie_Escape_Revised_Scenarios.docx`. They do **not** change the game itself
(`content/scenarios.json` is untouched).

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `handwritten.py` | Hand-written additions: flags that pay off later, conditional options, rewritten final gates, 5 new data scenes |
| `minigames_new.py` | The 10 realistic mini games and where each plays in the story |
| `revise.py` | Applies the rule-based changes (trade-offs, traps/gems, weather corrections, weather-adjusted ratings) and writes `revised.json` |
| `build_doc.js` | Builds the Word doc from `revised.json` and `minigames.json` |
| `build_breakdown_doc.js` | Builds `Zombie_Escape_Game_Breakdown.docx` (needs `/tmp/docdata.json`; see the comment at its top) |

Rebuild (needs Python 3.10+ and Node.js with `npm install docx`):

```bash
cd scenario_revisions
python revise.py
python -c "import json, minigames_new as m; json.dump({'rules': m.SHARED_RULES, 'games': m.GAMES, 'placement': m.PLACEMENT}, open('minigames.json','w'), indent=1)"
node build_doc.js
```

// Builds the Game Breakdown Word doc. Its input, /tmp/docdata.json, was generated in the chat from the game data (routes, SEIR results, mc_results.json).
const fs = require("fs");
const D = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("/tmp/docdata.json", "utf8"));
const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, WidthType, ShadingType, BorderStyle,
  HeadingLevel, PageOrientation, AlignmentType, Footer, PageNumber, TableOfContents, PageBreak } = require("docx");

const W = 13680; // landscape letter, 0.75" margins
const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 4, color: "B7C3CC" };
const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
const P = (text, opts = {}) => new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 120 }, ...opts, children: [new TextRun({ text, ...(opts.run || {}) })] });
const H1 = (t) => new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun(t)] });
const H2 = (t) => new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, children: [new TextRun(t)] });
let tno = 0;
function T(title, headers, rows, fr) {
  tno += 1;
  const tot = fr.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const widths = fr.map((f) => Math.floor(W * f / tot));
  widths[widths.length - 1] += W - widths.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const cell = (txt, i, head, shade) => new TableCell({
    borders, width: { size: widths[i], type: WidthType.DXA },
    shading: head ? { fill: "1F2F3D", type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto" } : shade ? { fill: "EEF2F5", type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: "auto" } : undefined,
    margins: { top: 50, bottom: 50, left: 90, right: 90 },
    children: String(txt).split("\n").map((line) => new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: line, size: 17, bold: head, color: head ? "FFFFFF" : "1A1A1A", font: "Arial" })] })),
  });
  return [
    new Paragraph({ keepNext: true, spacing: { before: 200, after: 80 }, children: [new TextRun({ text: `Table ${tno}. ${title}`, bold: true, size: 20, color: "C25E00" })] }),
    new Table({ width: { size: W, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: widths,
      rows: [new TableRow({ tableHeader: true, children: headers.map((h, i) => cell(h, i, true)) }),
        ...rows.map((r, k) => new TableRow({ cantSplit: true, children: r.map((v, i) => cell(v, i, false, k % 2 === 1)) }))] }),
    new Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 120 }, children: [] }),
  ];
}
const pct = (v, d = 1) => (v * 100).toFixed(d) + "%";
const kids = [];
const add = (...x) => x.flat().forEach((y) => kids.push(y));

// ---------------- title
add(new Paragraph({ alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT, spacing: { after: 60 }, children: [new TextRun({ text: "Zombie Escape", bold: true, size: 56, color: "1F2F3D" })] }),
